# Infosys Q4 FY26: Headcount falls by 8,440, attrition rises to 12.6%, profit at Rs 8,501 crore

**URL:** https://www.storyboard18.com/brand-marketing/infosys-q4-fy26-headcount-falls-by-8440-attrition-rises-to-12-6-profit-at-rs-8501-crore-96060.htm
**Description:** Infosys reported Q4 FY26 profit of Rs 8,501 crore with margins improving, while headcount declined and attrition rose to 12.6 percent, CEO Salil Parekh said strong deal wins supported performance.
**Scraped:** 2026-11-17T15:04:45.717120+00:00

---

Infosys Ltd reported a consolidated net profit of Rs 8,501 crore for the January to March quarter, up 27.8 percent compared to the previous quarter. Revenue came in at Rs 46,402 crore, rising 2 percent sequentially, according to its consolidated financial statement.

At the operating level, earnings before interest and tax stood at Rs 9,743 crore. The operating margin improved to 21 percent from 18.4 percent in the December quarter. Profit before tax was reported at Rs 10,797 crore, while lower tax expenses supported the growth in profit. Earnings per share increased to Rs 21.01 from Rs 16.17 in the previous quarter.

**Hiring and attrition**

The company’s workforce declined during the quarter, reversing a six-quarter trend of sequential additions. Infosys reduced its headcount by 8,440 employees in the January to March period, taking the total employee base to 328,594.

Voluntary attrition in the IT services segment increased to 12.6 percent, up from 12.3 percent in the previous quarter, indicating a slight rise in exits.

Jayesh Sanghrajka, Chief Financial Officer, [Infosys](https://www.storyboard18.com/amp/brand-marketing/openai-partners-infosys-to-scale-enterprise-ai-deployment-95976.htm), said “Our headcount sequentially has gone down, but on a YoY basis it has gone up by 5,000 people. There’s always some quarterly seasonality. Headcount is a function of utilisation and the volumes we see. This quarter the volumes were softer, plus the freshers in the system had to be accounted for.”

**Deal wins and business performance**

Large deal total contract value for the quarter stood at 3.2 billion dollars, while full-year deal wins were at 14.9 billion dollars.

“We delivered a resilient performance in FY 26 with growth of 3.1% with strong large deal wins of $14.9 billion, reflecting the robustness of our enterprise AI value proposition and market share gains in large transformation opportunities. The simplicity and strength of our AI services strategy across six areas is gaining traction in the market further strengthened by strong ecosystem AI partnerships enabling clients to get value from AI”, said Salil Parekh, Chief Executive Officer and Managing Director.

“Our AI First value framework and differentiated Topaz Fabric, position us uniquely to deepen client trust and gain greater share of the market”, he added

**Dividend and guidance**

[Infosys](https://www.storyboard18.com/brand-marketing/infosys-flags-zero-tolerance-after-pune-bpm-harassment-claims-go-viral-ws-l-95177.htm) announced a final dividend of Rs 25 per equity share for FY26.

For FY27, the company guided for revenue growth of 1.5 percent to 3.5 percent in constant currency, widening its earlier range, indicating a cautious near-term outlook. The company said demand remains affected by lower discretionary spending and macroeconomic challenges in key markets.

**Fresher hiring plan**

Infosys had earlier outlined its hiring plans for fresh graduates. In January 2026, CEO Parekh told Moneycontrol on the sidelines of the World Economic Forum in Davos that the company plans to recruit 20,000 college graduates in FY27.

The company had already onboarded around 18,000 freshers in the first three quarters of FY26, and had indicated it would close the year with a total of 20,000 campus hires. During the third quarter of FY26, Infosys had also reported a net addition of more than 5,000 employees.
